tone_statements.citation: Tạ Quang Tùng. 2018. Chữ viết các dân tộc thiểu số ở Việt Nam với việc biên soạn từ điển (trường hợp tiếng Kháng) [Writing systems for ethnic minorities in Vietnam and dictionary compilation: the case of Khang]. Từ điển học & Bách khoa thư [Lexicography & Encyclopedia] 2018, số 2 (52): 49-56.
tone_statements.quote: Tiếng Kháng có hệ thống âm vị khá phong phú, hệ thống nguyên âm trong tiếng Kháng có sự đối lập về trường độ, là ngôn ngữ có thanh điệu [3] [6]. [...] 3.5. Cách ghi thanh điệu. Thanh 1: ngang bằng - cao. Ký hiệu là (44). Thanh 2: xuống - thấp. Ký hiệu là (31). Thanh 3: xuống lên - cao. Ký hiệu là (323). Thanh 4: xuống lên - thấp. Ký hiệu là (212). Thanh 5: lên - cao. Ký hiệu là (35), hoặc (44) trong âm tiết khép. Thanh 6: ngang thấp - bằng. Ký hiệu là (22), hoặc (11) trong âm tiết khép.
tone_statements.translation: Khang has a fairly rich phoneme system; the Khang vowel system has a length opposition; it is a language with tones [3] [6]. [...] 3.5. Writing the tones. Tone 1: level - high. Symbol (44). Tone 2: falling - low. Symbol (31). Tone 3: falling-rising - high. Symbol (323). Tone 4: falling-rising - low. Symbol (212). Tone 5: rising - high. Symbol (35), or (44) in checked syllables. Tone 6: low level. Symbol (22), or (11) in checked syllables.
tone_statements.locator: p. 51 §3.1.1 and p. 54 §3.5 'Cách ghi thanh điệu', with Bảng 6 on p. 56; a few vowel glyphs are mis-encoded in the (e.g. 'thҩp' for 'thấp') and are given here
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

tone_statements.citation: Tạ Quang Tùng. 2016. Hệ thống thanh điệu tiếng Kháng (trên cơ sở cứ liệu phân tích bằng máy tính) [Tone system in Khang language (based on computerized analysis)]. Ngôn ngữ & Đời sống [Language & Life] 2016, số 2 (244): 95-100.
tone_statements.quote: Abstract: This research is conducted to describe tone system in Khang language, a language belonging to Austroasiatic language family, Mon - Khmer subgroup, Khmuic brach. By using speech analyser softwares, all the phonetic features of tones are analysed such as: waveforms, spectrogram, spectra, intensity, basic formants, duration,... [...] 5. Ket lu^n Trong cfic ngdn ngtt dang dugc xip vao nhinh Khmuic, tiing Khang 14 mgt trudng hgp dfic bift: 14 ngdn ngtt cd thanh difu v4 cd tdi 6 thanh difu.
tone_statements.translation: [conclusion] Among the languages currently placed in the Khmuic branch, Khang is a special case: it is a tone language, and has as many as 6 tones.
tone_statements.locator: p. 95 and p. 100 §5 'Kết luận'; tone value tables pp. 97 and 99; the Vietnamese body's is a diacritic-less legacy and the §5 sentence is quoted exactly

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. 2010. The Kháng language of Vietnam in comparison to Ksingmul (Xinh-mun). In K. A. McElhanon & G. Reesink (eds.), A Mosaic of languages and cultures: studies celebrating the career of Karl J. Franklin, 138-154. SIL e-Books 19. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: No Kháng-specific stress statement. §1 has only the family-level remark that Mon-Khmer word shapes are 'weak-syllable (with reduction of vocalic and prosodic features) + strong-syllable'; §2-2.1 say Kháng 'shows only vestiges of the original sesquisyllabic pattern' (ʔbu./sa./ma. presyllables in animal and nature words); §3 'Kháng/Bumang syllables and tone' describes six tones with F0 plots. Than Uyên (Lai Châu) variety; Bumang data from Dao Jie.

sources.citation: Tạ Quang Tùng. 2021. A Phonology and Lexicon of Khang in Vietnam. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society (JSEALS) 14.2: i-xxix. hdl:10524/52487 (CC-BY).
sources.note: Nothing: the words stress/accent/prominence do not occur. §3 gives the word template (C1ə̌/ǎ).C2(C3)V(C4)T, says 99.45% of the 917-item lexicon is monosyllabic and only five words have a presyllable (with extra-short /ə̌/ or /ǎ/); §6 describes eight lexical tones (six on sonorant-final, two on stop-final syllables) plus voice-register correlates. Nam Mu village variety (Tuần Giáo, Điện Biên).

sources.citation: Sidwell, Paul. 2014. Khmuic classification and homeland. Mon-Khmer Studies 43.1: 47-56.
sources.note: Nothing; lexical-classification paper arguing Khang and Khabit are Palaungic. Cites Mikami 2003 as the Khang data source.

sources.note: States Khang has a rich phoneme inventory, a vowel-length contrast and is a tone language; §3.5 and Bảng 6 give six tones with Chao values and proposed Quốc-ngữ-style tone marks: T1 high level (44, unmarked), T2 low falling (31, huyền), T3 high falling-rising (323, ngã), T4 low falling-rising (212, hỏi), T5 high rising (35; 44 in checked syllables, sắc), T6 low level (22; 11 in checked syllables, nặng) - i.e. 6 tonemes with checked-syllable variants; cites Tạ 2016 for the analysis.

sources.citation: Nguyễn Văn Lợi & Tạ Quang Tùng. 2019. Phonetic system of Khang Quang Lam. Paper presented at The GLOCAL Conference on Asian Linguistic Anthropology (CALA) 2019, Paññāsāstra University of Cambodia, Siem Reap, 23-26 January 2019 (General Session, 'Documenting Language'). Abstract no. 272.
sources.note: Conference abstract only: says Khang as a whole is tending from a non-tonal to a tonal language (tonogenesis); no tone inventory and no statement on whether Quang Lam itself has tones.

tone.quote: The report presents the characteristics of the current Khang Quang Lam phonetic system (data surveyed in 2017), in comparison with the Khang Quang Lam phonetic system 25 years ago (data surveyed in 1990) ... At the same time, indicating the phonetic tendency in Khang: 1- monosyllabisation; 2 – From non-tonal language to tonal language. Keywords: Khang Quang Lam; Lexical and Phonetic Computerized Database; The method of phonetico-phonological analysis of computerized database; Monosyllabisation; The process of forming tones
tone.locator: abstract, second paragraph and keywords line (GLOCAL abstract web page, unpaginated)
